owner: CC owns the retirement mechanics. Akien owns the design decision that corrections-as-training-data replaces approve/disprove.

questions.a: CLI RETIRES, PRIMITIVE STAYS: cairn recordverdict (the CLI face) retires. learning_block.record_verdict (the primitive) stays until the dial migrates. Two retirements, sequenced.

BINARY SIGNAL vs CORRECTIONS-AS-DATA: recordverdict captured approve/disprove + verbatim — the binary was the signal, words were metadata. cairn review captures words as the signal. The inversion is the design shift.
RETIREMENT IS LIFECYCLE, NOT FAILURE: recordverdict-cli-door (PROVED) was correct when built. The design moved on. The proof was valid; the need changed.

workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> [PROVED] (PROVED 2026-08-29: retirement note on bin/cmd/recordverdict naming cairn review. Retirement field on recordverdict-cli-door ticket. No gate reads approve/disprove binary. Proof green x2, sealed netns. Verdict answers chart 3/3.)
watchme: none, because the retirement is a one-time state change. cairn review's efficacy is monitored by the skill_block's dial (skilldial.py). The proof at bin/proofs/test_cairn_command.py covers the command.
